```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
```

`pbn::table1()` computes the numbers of a descriptive table. A style formats these numbers as the text that a journal or a report needs. With a style, the output gets the columns `row`, `value_pretty` and `p_pretty`. A style can also add a heading row and a Missing row to a variable.

## What a style is

A style is a YAML file of pbn, `inst/table1/<name>_<YYYY_MM_DD>.yml`. Give its name, the file name without `.yml`, to the argument `style` of `table1()`. pbn never edits a released style. A changed style gets a new file with a new date, so a project that names a style gets the same text at each run.

Each field of a style holds a `value` and a `source`. The source says where the value comes from. It is the guide of a journal and its count of papers, the guideline and its page, or `editorial choice`.

## The schema

This style file has every field. The section Styles of `?table1` gives the type and the check of each field. The fields `cont.median_digits`, `missing.row_template` and `missing.row_pct_digits`, and the section `cat`, are optional.

```{cat, engine.opts = list(file = file.path(tempdir(), "example_2026_12_01.yml"), lang = "yaml")}
bin:
  template: {value: "{events} ({pct})", source: editorial choice}
  pct_digits: {value: 1, source: editorial choice}
cont:
  template: {value: "{median} ({q1}-{q3})", source: editorial choice}
  mean_digits: {value: 1, source: editorial choice}
  sd_digits: {value: 1, source: editorial choice}
  median_digits: {value: 1, source: editorial choice}
cat:
  template: {value: "{events} ({pct})", source: editorial choice}
  pct_digits: {value: 1, source: editorial choice}
  heading_template: {value: "", source: editorial choice}
p:
  digits: {value: 3, source: editorial choice}
  template: {value: "P ={p}", source: editorial choice}
  lower: {value: 0.001, source: editorial choice}
  below_template: {value: "P <{lower}", source: editorial choice}
  upper: {value: 0.999, source: editorial choice}
  above_template: {value: "P >{upper}", source: editorial choice}
thousands:
  mark: {value: ",", source: editorial choice}
  from: {value: 10000, source: editorial choice}
missing:
  show: {value: row_if_any, source: editorial choice}
  template: {value: "; {missing} missing", source: editorial choice}
  row_template: {value: "{missing} ({pct})", source: editorial choice}
  row_pct_digits: {value: 1, source: editorial choice}
footnotes:
  - {value: "Values are n (percent) or median (quartiles).", source: editorial choice}
```

The fake data below have 12,000 rows in two groups. `education` is a `"cat"` variable with three levels and 60 missing values. `wide()` puts one printed row on each row and one group in each column.

```{r}
set.seed(1)
n <- 12000
d <- data.table::data.table(
  group = rep(c("Control", "Exposed"), times = c(9000, 3000)),
  smoker = stats::rbinom(n, 1, 0.15),
  age = round(stats::rnorm(n, mean = 31, sd = 5), 1),
  education = factor(
    sample(c("Primary", "Secondary", "Tertiary"), n, replace = TRUE),
    levels = c("Primary", "Secondary", "Tertiary")
  )
)
d$smoker[sample(n, 40)] <- NA
d$education[sample(n, 60)] <- NA
vars <- data.table::data.table(
  var = c("smoker", "age"),
  type = c("bin", "cont")
)
vars_cat <- rbind(vars, data.table::data.table(var = "education", type = "cat"))

# One printed row for each "value", "heading" and "missing" row of the "All"
# group, and the groups in the order of t1.
wide <- function(t1) {
  all <- t1$grp == "All"
  label <- t1$var
  label[!is.na(t1$level)] <- paste("-", t1$level[!is.na(t1$level)])
  label[t1$row == "missing"] <- "- Missing"
  out <- data.frame(row = label[all])
  for (g in unique(t1$grp)) {
    out[[g]] <- t1$value_pretty[t1$grp == g]
  }
  out$p <- t1$p_pretty[all]
  return(out)
}

t1 <- pbn::table1(
  d,
  by = "group",
  vars = vars_cat,
  style = file.path(tempdir(), "example_2026_12_01.yml")
)
knitr::kable(wide(t1))
attr(t1, "footnotes")
```

The level rows of `education` divide by the non-missing count of the group. Its Missing row divides by every row of the group.

## The installed styles

The tables below show `smoker` and `age` only. A style without the section `cat` cannot format a `"cat"` variable.

```{r, results = "asis", echo = FALSE}
styles <- pbn::table1_styles()
if (length(styles) == 0) {
  cat("pbn", format(utils::packageVersion("pbn")), "installs no style.\n")
}
for (s in styles) {
  t1 <- pbn::table1(d, by = "group", vars = vars, style = s)
  cat("\n### ", s, "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(knitr::kable(wide(t1)))
  cat("\n", paste0(attr(t1, "footnotes"), "\n\n"), sep = "")
}
```
